clues.title: Plate: Yellow plates
text: If you see yellow license plates on both the front and back in Europe with a super flat landscape, it’s likely the Netherlands. Luxembourg also uses all-yellow plates but is much hillier. Denmark may have yellow plates for commercial vehicles, so use other clues like architecture, bike lanes, and surroundings to confirm it’s the Netherlands.

Many roads have dashed outside lines.
Sometimes, you can find unique green middle lines.

clues.title: Landscape: Flevoland
text: Almost all of the land belonging to the province of Flevoland was reclaimed from the sea in the mid-20th century. As a result, the province has a distinct, man-made look: extremely straight roads and large crop fields dominate the landscape. Wind turbines are common.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Polder
text: Most of the west and north is at or below sea-level. As a result, most of this region’s countryside has a distinct “polder” landscape: the landscape is marshy, often with a large amount of small waterways.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: Yellow Plates
text: The Netherlands has long, yellow licence plates with the standard European blue strip on the left.
Dutch taxis have blue plates.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Bollards
text: The Netherlands has a simple, white bollard with a red reflector.
On rare occasions, you can find round French-style bollards with a red band and a pointed top.
A difference with French bollards is that the red wrap usually does not go all the way around the bollard.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Large Power Lines
text: The Netherlands usually does not have any utility poles.
You might see larger power lines like the ones shown in the image, but essentially never any street-level smaller utility poles.
Belgium does use utility poles somewhat commonly.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Rumble Strips
text: Many rural roads feature a sort of brick rumble strip on the sides.
This is fairly unique to the Netherlands and a good way to identify the country in very rural rounds.

clues.title: Landscape: Flat Landscape
text: The Netherlands is extraordinarily flat.
In most of the country, you will get no more than a few metres of elevation.
Large swathes of the country are reclaimed land that is at or even below sea level.

clues.title: Brick Roads
text: Brick roads are common in the Netherlands, both in rural and urban areas.
The brick pattern shown in the image is especially common.

clues.title: Bicycle Paths
text: Many Dutch roads are flanked by bicycle paths.
Different designs exist, but a very common one is a reddish-pink lane.
Cycling is one of the most common modes of transportation in the Netherlands.
You will see cyclists and bicycles everywhere.

clues.title: Architecture: Row Houses
text: As mentioned before, row houses are very common in the Netherlands.
Almost half of the Dutch housing stock are row houses, significantly more than almost all other European countries.

clues.title: Architecture: South - Rolling Shutters
text: Rolling shutters on house windows are more common in the southern half of the Netherlands.
While more prevalent in the south, rolling shutters on homes in more northern regions are not unheard of.
Use this meta with some caution.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Red-Brownish Bricks
text: Brick architecture is very common in the Netherlands.
Many buildings feature red-brownish-coloured bricks.
Roofs often have orange or dark grey tiles.
Similar brick architecture is also common in Denmark and Belgium.

clues.title: Netherlands
text: Dutch landline phone numbers start with a three- or four-digit area code. These are geographically grouped, except for the ones that start with 07, and two of the 02 codes.
NOTE: Dutch mobile phone numbers start with 06, which is a code that is not used for any of the landline area codes.

clues.title: Plate: Netherlands
text: The Netherlands has long, yellow licence plates with the standard European blue strip on the left. Dutch taxis have blue plates.

NOTE: The only other countries in Europe with yellow licence plates are Luxembourg and the UK. For the UK, only the back plates are yellow, and they often lack the blue strip. In addition, some older coverage in France features the French yellow back plates. In Denmark, you can find yellow plates on commercial vehicles.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Rotterdam vibes
text: If you know your in The Netherlands, and you see many tall buildings, you will most likely be in Rotterdam. This city has the majority of skyscrapers within The Netherlands.
NOTE: The Hague and Amsterdam also have some tall buildings but not as much as Rotterdam.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Language: Dutch
text: Dutch is a Germanic language related to German. Dutch features a lot of double vowels. Typical letter clusters are **ij, ieuw** and **oe**. “**IJ**“ written as one capitalised letter is also unique to the language.
The Dutch name for street is **straat**.
The Dutch name for road is **weg** (same as German).
NOTE: Dutch is also spoken in the northern Flanders region of Belgium.
